title: OGC API – MCP Mapping Specification
description: A formal, machine-readable specification that translates core functionality of OGC APIs into MCP tool concepts. Enables LLM agents to interact with any OGC-compliant server through a unified, natural-language-friendly interface.

module.description: Which OGC API module this tool belongs to

description.description: Human and LLM readable description of what this tool does

natural_language_triggers.description: Example phrases that should trigger this tool

prerequisites.description: Tool IDs that should typically be called before this one

path_template.description: URL path with {placeholders} for path parameters

summary_fields.description: Fields to extract and present to the LLM — avoid dumping full raw response

followup_tools.description: Tools that can naturally follow this one

processes.title: OGC API – Processes
processes.description: Enables execution of geospatial and analytical processes on a server. Use for any computation, analysis, or transformation of spatial data.

tools.description: Lists all geospatial processes available on this OGC API server. Use this when the user asks what the system can do, what analyses are available, or whether a specific process exists. This should be called first when exploring capabilities.
natural_language_triggers: show me what tools are available

output_schema.description: List of available processes with their IDs, titles, and descriptions

errors.plain_english: Authentication required. Please log in to access processes.
Cannot reach the OGC API server. Check that the server is running.
errors.llm_action: Inform the user and suggest checking the server

tools.description: Gets the full description of a specific process including its required inputs, expected outputs, and what it does. Always call this before executing a process you have not used before.
natural_language_triggers: tell me more about the X process
what does the X process do

parameters.name: process_id
parameters.description: The ID of the process to describe

output_schema.description: Full process metadata including input schema and output schema

errors.plain_english: Process not found. The process ID may be incorrect.
errors.llm_action: Call processes_list to show available process IDs

tools.description: Executes a process synchronously and returns the result immediately. Use for quick processes where the result is expected within seconds. Do not use Prefer: respond-async header.

parameters.name: process_id
parameters.description: The ID of the process to execute

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: Process-specific inputs as defined by the process description. Must match the input schema returned by processes_describe.

output_schema.description: Process result — format depends on process type. Buffer returns GeoJSON Feature. Zonal stats returns statistics object.

errors.plain_english: Invalid inputs. One or more required inputs are missing or have wrong types.
errors.llm_action: Call processes_describe to check the required input schema and try again

errors.plain_english: The process failed on the server.
errors.llm_action: Inform the user and suggest checking input values

tools.description: Executes a process asynchronously. Returns a job ID immediately. Use for long-running processes. After calling this, use jobs_get_status to monitor progress and jobs_get_results when complete.

parameters.name: process_id
parameters.description: The ID of the process to execute

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: Process-specific inputs matching the process input schema

output_schema.description: Job submission confirmation with jobID for tracking

errors.llm_action: Call processes_describe to verify required inputs

tools.description: Lists all submitted jobs and their current status. Use when the user wants to check on previous jobs or see what analyses have been run.

output_schema.description: List of jobs with IDs, process names, status, and timestamps

tools.description: Gets the current status of a specific job. Poll this after submitting an async job until status is successful or failed.
natural_language_triggers: what is the status of job X

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job UUID returned by processes_execute_async

output_schema.description: Job status including progress percentage and timestamps

errors.plain_english: Job not found. It may have been deleted.
errors.llm_action: Call jobs_list to show available jobs

tools.description: Retrieves the output of a completed job. Only call this when jobs_get_status shows status as successful.
natural_language_triggers: get the results of job X

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job UUID of the completed job

output_schema.description: The process output. Format depends on process type.

errors.plain_english: Results not found. The job may not be complete yet.
errors.llm_action: Call jobs_get_status first to verify the job is successful

tools.description: Dismisses and deletes a job and its results. Call this after retrieving results to clean up.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job UUID to delete

output_schema.description: Confirmation that the job was deleted

errors.plain_english: Job not found. It may already have been deleted.
errors.llm_action: Inform the user the job does not exist

features.title: OGC API – Features
features.description: Provides access to vector geospatial data — points, lines, and polygons. Use for querying buildings, roads, lakes, boundaries, and any other geographic features.

tools.description: Lists all available feature collections on the OGC API – Features server. Use this first to discover what datasets are available before querying.
natural_language_triggers: what geographic data can I query

output_schema.description: List of collections with IDs, titles, and descriptions

errors.llm_action: Check server URL and try again

tools.description: Gets detailed information about a specific feature collection including its geographic extent, attributes, and coordinate system.
natural_language_triggers: tell me about the X dataset

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The collection ID from features_list_collections

output_schema.description: Collection metadata including bounding box, CRS, and links

errors.llm_action: Call features_list_collections to show valid collection IDs

tools.description: Fetches features from a collection. Can filter by geographic area (bbox) or limit results. Use for retrieving actual geographic data — roads, buildings, lakes, boundaries.
natural_language_triggers: show me X in this area
get all X within this bbox
retrieve features from the X dataset

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The collection to query

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Bounding box filter as minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of features to return

output_schema.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection with matching features and their properties

errors.plain_english: Invalid query parameters. Check bbox format.
errors.llm_action: Verify bbox is in minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat format
Call features_list_collections to show valid IDs

tools.description: Gets the complete details and geometry of a single feature by its ID. Use this when you need the exact geometry of a feature to pass into another operation such as zonal statistics or buffer analysis.
natural_language_triggers: I need the boundary of X

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The collection the feature belongs to

parameters.name: feature_id
parameters.description: The ID of the specific feature

output_schema.description: Complete GeoJSON Feature with full geometry and all properties

errors.llm_action: Call features_get_items to find valid feature IDs

records.title: OGC API – Records
records.description: Provides access to metadata catalogues for discovering available geospatial datasets. Use this FIRST when the user wants to find data — before querying Features or EDR.

tools.description: Lists all available catalogue collections on the OGC API – Records server. Use this first to discover what catalogues are available.

output_schema.description: List of catalogue collections with IDs and descriptions

errors.llm_action: Check server URL and inform the user

tools.description: Searches a geospatial catalogue for datasets by keyword or geographic area. This should be the first step when a user wants to find data — use it to discover what is available before querying Features or EDR. If a keyword returns no results, try broader synonyms automatically.
natural_language_triggers: look up X in the catalogue

parameters.name: catalogue_id
parameters.description: The catalogue collection ID from records_list_collections

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: Search term to find relevant datasets. If no results, try broader synonyms.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: Geographic filter as minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum records to return

output_schema.description: List of matching dataset records with titles, descriptions, and metadata

errors.plain_english: No datasets found for that search term.
errors.llm_action: Try a broader synonym automatically before telling the user

tools.description: Gets complete metadata for a specific catalogue record including download links, data format, coordinate system, temporal coverage, and data provider.
natural_language_triggers: show me the metadata for X
what format is dataset X in

parameters.name: catalogue_id
parameters.description: The catalogue collection ID

parameters.name: record_id
parameters.description: The record ID from records_search results

output_schema.description: Full record metadata including links, format, CRS, temporal coverage, keywords

errors.llm_action: Call records_search to find valid record IDs

server_capability_negotiation.description: Before calling any tool, the proxy must check the server's /conformance endpoint to verify it supports the required operation. If a capability is not supported, the LLM must adapt its approach.
server_capability_negotiation.behaviour: If server does not support CQL2 filters, fall back to bbox-only queries. If server does not support async execution, use sync. Never fail silently.

pagination.description: OGC API responses are paginated. The proxy must handle multi-page results transparently.
pagination.detection: Check for 'next' link in response links array
pagination.behaviour: For LLM consumption, fetch first page only and indicate total count. For complete results, follow next links automatically up to a configurable maximum.

crs_handling.description: All spatial operations must use consistent coordinate reference systems.
crs_handling.behaviour: Always request data in EPSG:4326. If server returns different CRS, transform before returning to LLM. Never pass raw degree values to metric operations without reprojection.

format_negotiation.description: Always request JSON format for LLM consumption.
format_negotiation.behaviour: Always append ?f=json to all GET requests. Never request HTML format for programmatic use.

response_summarisation.description: Raw OGC API responses can be very large and exceed LLM context windows. The proxy must summarise before passing to the LLM.
rules: Never pass raw GeoJSON with more than 20 coordinate pairs directly to the LLM
Summarise feature lists to ID, type, and key properties only
For statistics results, present all values clearly formatted
Always include total count even when returning partial results
Store full responses in proxy memory for follow-up tool calls

authentication.description: Credential management is handled by the proxy layer. The LLM never sees or manages credentials.
authentication.behaviour: Inject credentials automatically on every request. Refresh tokens before expiry. On 401 response, attempt token refresh once before failing.

error_translation.description: All HTTP errors must be translated to plain English before reaching the LLM.

extensibility.description: New OGC API modules can be added without modifying existing modules.
instructions: Add a new entry under 'modules' with a unique module ID
Define tools following the tool schema in definitions
Register the module in the proxy's module registry
